newsitem.title: USA: AlliedSignal unit buys Echlin brake business.
newsitem.headline: AlliedSignal unit buys Echlin brake business.

text.p: AlliedSignal Automotive and its truck partner, Germany's Knorr-Bremse AG, said Monday they agreed to buy the heavy-truck air brake systems business of Echlin Inc. for undisclosed terms.

AlliedSignal Automotive said long with Eclin's truck brake busines in the United States and Europe, it also will acquire Echlin's U.S.-based commercial vehicle friction materials and aftermarket brake shoe relining operations.
The businesses to be acquired employ about 2,300 people and have sales of about $320 million.

AlliedSignal and Knorr-Bremse operate truck air brake joint ventures in North America, South America and Europe with combined 1996 sales of about $800 million. The joint ventures currently operate five major facilities in North America and nine in Europe, with about 5,000 employees.

"Echlin's truck brake business -- known as Midland Brake Inc. in the U.S. and Grau in Europe -- is an excellent strategic fit, which will strengthen our ability to serve aftermarket customers, truck and trailer manufacturers, and vehicle users," said John Barter, president of AlliedSignal Automotive.
AlliedSignal automotive is a unit of Morristown, N.J.-based AlliedSignal Inc., whose businesses include aerospace and automotive products, chemicals, fibers and plastics.
Midland Brake Inc., based in Kansas City, Mo., has manufacturing plants in Kansas, Tennessee, North Carolina and Oklahoma, plus parts distribution centres in Missouri and Canada.

Under the deal AlliedSignal would gain access to Echlin's North American aftermarket distribution network, as well as rights to the Midland, Maxi-Brake, Berg, and Like-Nu trademarks which would complement AlliedSignal's Bendix brand.
The companies expect the transaction to close in the spring.
